messages:
maya: Heads up — provisioning failures in us-west2 since ~03:00 UTC. Scale-up for gpu-pool-small is hitting NVMe write latency spikes and a few nodes went readonly. Seen ~25% attach failures and a couple of OOMs.

jorge: Which fleet exactly? any obvious diffs in images or job mix?

maya: gpu-pool-small (preemptible-batch). Suspect write amplification during container copy-up. We pushed a model image yesterday with two new large files (~5GB each) into /var/models.

maya: dmesg snippets: ```
[12345.678901] nvme0n1: write_latency_ms=1200 io_err=EIO
[12345.679012] overlayfs: copy-up failed, write returned -5
[12346.000000] EXT4-fs error (device nvme0n1p1): ext4_journal_start_sb: Detected aborted journal
```

liam: Overlayfs copy-up + big image deltas = massive temporary writes. If copy-up happens concurrently with janitor scrubs we can easily blow past device queue depth and thermal limits.

anika: We have ephemeral-scrub jobs running in the same window (02:50-03:10 UTC) with default concurrency=40. That will definitely contend with copy-up.

sre-bot: :warning: Alert fired: provisioner.scaleup.fail_rate > 20% in us-west2 (alert-1234)

ops-runner: Immediate mitigations we can try: pause non-critical batch jobs for 2h, reduce scrub concurrency, and if needed bring up buffer nodes (reserve capacity). Short-term pause avoids more read-only reassigns.

jorge: Can we throttle copy-up or use a different mount option? Kernel-level changes are risky; prefer application-level mitigations first. Any chance the image push triggered the change in copy-up frequency?

maya: Confirmed image push at 01:40 UTC. Most scale-ups happen around 03:00 when nightly batch starts. Timing overlaps.

liam: Proposal: 1) Reduce scrub concurrency from 40 -> 6 on a canary subset (5% of nodes) 2) Pause non-essential batch jobs for 120m 3) Add a soft circuit-breaker: if node_nvme_latency_95 > 500ms then prevent new scale-ups to that rack.

anika: I can change janitor config now and schedule the canary at 04:00 UTC. Metrics to watch: node_nvme_latency_95, provisioning_fail_rate, overlay_copyup_errors.

ops-runner: Medium-term: reserve spare capacity in us-west2 (proposal: 20-30 GPUs). Rough cost: ~ $8.5k - $12k/month depending on instance type. That buys us breathing room for deploys.

jorge: If reducing scrub concurrency fixes it, let's keep that as default until we finish a deeper analysis on overlay behavior. Also add histogram buckets for copy-up write sizes in our exporter.

maya: I'll open a rollbackable PR to change scrub concurrency and add the canary selection label. PR: infra/ops#789. Kicking canary at 04:00.

liam: Also update alerting: suppress noisy per-node NVMe warnings during the canary but escalate if provisioner.fail_rate > 10% cluster-wide.

anika: I'll update the janitor config and add a runbook entry for this pattern (overlay copy-up + scrub overlap).

ops-runner: If the canary fails to improve after 30m, we execute plan B: reserve 20 GPUs and throttle batch job ingress.

maya: Acknowledged. I'll push the PR, start the canary at 04:00, and paste dashboards in this thread.

jorge: Thanks — nice triage. :thumbsup:

liam: quick checklist for PR: include metrics to monitor, rollback steps, and a smoke test (scale-up 10 nodes).

maya: Will do. Creating ticket and runbook now. Tagging everyone in the follow-ups.

anika: :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Note: incident-created incident-2026-03-20-usw2-nvme-provisioning (assigned: ops-runner)

ops-runner: Logged cost/impact note in the incident. Will update if we need reserved capacity.

maya: Closing loop later with postmortem if this persists. For now, canary + scrub throttle scheduled.
